result:
Comment authors can now edit their own comments. I haven't run tests, lint, type-check or the app, as you asked.

- **API:** `features/comments/api/update-comment.ts` sends `PATCH /comments/{commentId}` with `{ body }`. The `useUpdateComment` hook refreshes the comment list via `getInfiniteCommentsQueryOptions(discussionId).queryKey`. It also shows the "Comment Updated" success notification from inside the hook, as `CLAUDE.md` requires. The existing create and delete components call `useNotifications` themselves, so I didn't copy that pattern.
- **UI:** `features/comments/components/update-comment.tsx` adds an "Edit Comment" button that opens a form drawer. The drawer has a textarea pre-filled with the current body.
- **Visibility:** I added a `comment:update` policy in `lib/authorization.tsx` that is true only when the comment's author is the current user. Admins don't get the Edit button on other people's comments, although they can still delete them. `comments-list.tsx` wraps the button in `Authorization` with that policy.
- **Mock API:** I added a `PATCH /comments/:commentId` handler in `testing/mocks/handlers/comments.ts`, limited to the author's own comments. Without it the button would fail against the mock backend.

I made no changes to the Next.js apps.
